courses.subject: URBD
courses.title: Environmental & Urban Economics
courses.description: This course will study urban economic issues associated with environmental and social issues within urban regions. The course will study this topic from an interdisciplinary perspective. A range of topics in urban economics will be discussed including planning policies related to urban environment, migration, and transportation, as well as, zoning and liveability issues, and potentials for more sustainable, just and liveable cities. Students will become familiar with contemporary urban economic research and online sources of economic data. The course will prepare students to develop criteria for value judgments about the complex social, economic and environmental impact of urban design and planning.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students of MSc in Urban Design, MSc in Advanced Environmental Planning Technologies, and MSc in Landscape Architecture
courses.learning_outcomes:
On successful completion of this unit, students will be able to:
1. Demonstrate a basic understanding of the principles of macro and micro economic theory and the valuation of environmental resources.
2. Apply elementary methods of economic analysis to contemporary issues relating to the planning and management of built and natural environments.

courses.subject: URBD
courses.title: Topical Studies in Urban Design 3 - Urban Management
courses.description: This course provides a base for understanding urban management including the political and socio-economic aspects of urban development, governance issues, planning, policy framework and decision making within a Western and Asian development context. Through a series of lectures and seminars students are introduced to urban management methods and strategies in key areas such as land management, environmental management and public services delivery including associated problems and challenges within the context of Hong Kong and the GBA region.
courses.enrollment_requirement: For students of MSc in Urban Design.
courses.learning_outcomes: Students begin to appreciate the complex issues, problems and challenges of urban management of development within a city and regional context. Students gain an understanding of the methods and strategies used to overcome some of the challenges of urban management. Students learn the importance of collecting data to monitor, evaluate and manage urban development with regards to land, environment and infrastructure etc.
courses.course_syllabus: Through a series of lectures and seminars, students in this course are introduced to urban management by focusing on methods and strategies in key areas such as land management, environmental management and public services delivery in the context of Hong Kong and the Greater Bay Area.
